headline: Record shipments and pricing lift earnings sharply
summary_short: Q2 2026 net sales rose to $10.40B (+9% q/q) and diluted EPS jumped to $5.04 (+56.0% q/q) on a second consecutive quarterly record for steel mill shipments and higher realized pricing across all three segments.
summary_long: Steel mills pretax earnings rose to $1.56B from $1.13B q/q on higher average selling prices ($1,145/ton, +7% q/q) and volumes, plus a $130M cost-of-sales reduction from raw-materials procurement refunds. Steel products and raw materials earnings also rose on higher volumes/pricing. Net earnings included a $61M non-cash benefit ($0.20/share) from Nucor's Helion investment mark-up; adjusted diluted EPS was $4.84. Nucor returned $479M to shareholders via buybacks and dividends, holding $2.69B cash with an undrawn $2.25B revolver. Q3 2026 outlook: higher consolidated earnings expected on higher realized pricing in steel mills and steel products; raw materials earnings expected to decrease on lower margins.

drivers.explanation: Steel mills external average selling price rose 7% q/q to $1,145/ton and shipments were a second consecutive quarterly record; steel products volumes rose 11% q/q at stable pricing.
Higher steel mills earnings from pricing and volume, a $130M raw-materials procurement cost refund, and a $61M non-cash Helion investment mark-up drove the sequential EPS increase.
Segment earnings before tax rose across steel mills, steel products, and raw materials on higher pricing and volumes q/q, per the segment table.
Management attributes the result to investment across key U.S. economic sectors and supportive federal trade policy driving record steel mill shipments.
